# TherapyLog

> TherapyLog is a web-based TRT (testosterone replacement therapy) and peptide
> tracker for adults. It logs doses, models estimated serum levels from published
> half-lives, plans multi-compound syringe draws with compatibility rules, and
> tracks bloodwork against the reference range printed on the user's own lab
> report. Health data stays on the user's device. Free tier, no account required.

Site: https://therapylog.app/
Publisher: TherapyLog LLC, Floresville, Texas, USA
Contact: hello@therapylog.app

Disambiguation: "Therapylog" is also the name of an unrelated school-therapy
documentation product at therapylog.com. This is a different product. This one is
at therapylog.app and is a hormone-therapy and peptide tracker.

## Author and editorial policy

All reference content is written by Joel Gonzales, founder of TherapyLog. He is
not a clinician, and the site states that on every page. No clinical reviewer is
claimed. Claims cite primary literature or guideline documents; evidence is
labelled in three tiers (established clinical use, off-label or community
practice, animal-only or theoretical); the reference range printed on a user's
own lab report takes precedence over any generic range shown; optimal bands are
labelled non-diagnostic; every side-effect discussion ends with taking the result
to the prescribing clinician. The site sells software only, lists no vendor, and
takes no referral fee from any clinic, pharmacy or laboratory.

- /about/: Author, editorial policy, corrections process, and what the tools do
  and do not do.

- /: What TherapyLog is, who it is for, and pricing.
- /app: The tracker itself. Runs in the browser, installs to the home screen.
- /guide: Full user guide — every tab, control and workflow.
- /pro: The paid tier. Pro is $9.99/month or $99.99/year for managed AI; a
  bring-your-own-API-key plan is offered alongside it at a lower price. Paid
  features are the AI lab scanner and the AI assistant; the calculators, the
  compound reference and bloodwork logging are not behind the AI gate.

  listing; it is a web app installed to the home screen.

- /partnership: Affiliate and partner program.
- /directory/ and /providers/: Provider directory and provider signup.
- /privacy, /health-data-privacy, /terms: Legal policies.

## Free calculators (/tools/)

These pages are being published one at a time; the hub at /tools/ lists what is
live, and nothing below is linked until its page exists. Each calculator runs the
same function source as the app rather than a re-implementation — the source is
copied out of the app when the page is built and checked against it, so the two
cannot drift. All are free and need no account.

- Peptide reconstitution calculator: vial strength, diluent volume and target
  dose to draw volume in units and ml — and the reverse, solving for how much
  bacteriostatic water to add for a chosen draw.
- Per-compound reconstitution pages: the same calculator pre-filled, with a
  milligram-to-units ladder, the modelled half-life, and the storage rule.
- Insulin syringe unit converter: units to ml on U-100 syringes, with the
  half-unit rounding rule.
- Testosterone dose calculator: weekly dose split by injection frequency, with
  the modelled peak-to-trough swing per ester and cadence.
- Free testosterone calculator: Vermeulen calculated free and bioavailable
  testosterone from total testosterone, SHBG and albumin.
- Combined syringe planner: multi-compound draw planning with the compatibility
  rules (oil and water do not mix, suspensions draw alone, fragile proteins are
  not blended).
- Half-life calculator: single-dose and steady-state curves, time to steady
  state, accumulation ratio and peak-to-trough ratio. Estimated half-lives are
  labelled as estimates.
- Per-compound half-life pages: the curve, the numbers and their provenance.
- Combination checker ("can you take X with Y"): the interaction pairs the app
  knows about, with severity and reasoning. Not exhaustive and not a safety
  clearance.

## Lab marker reference (/markers/)

Marker pages are written with the assay method named wherever it changes the
interpretation — sensitive (LC/MS-MS) versus standard immunoassay estradiol,
direct versus calculated versus equilibrium-dialysis free testosterone, and so
on. Each carries the accepted units and their conversions, the generic reference
range labelled as generic, the non-diagnostic optimal band where one exists, and
authored explanation with primary sources. The working list, which is not a
publication schedule:

- estradiol, sensitive versus standard assay
- total testosterone, immunoassay versus LC/MS-MS
- free versus total testosterone
- SHBG
- hematocrit on testosterone therapy
- prolactin
- LH and FSH
- IGF-1
- HbA1c and fasting glucose
- ApoB versus LDL cholesterol
- lipoprotein(a)
- ferritin and the iron panel
- vitamin D
- the thyroid panel
- DHT
- a bloodwork checklist hub tying them together

## Disclaimer

TherapyLog is an informational tracking tool and is not a substitute for
professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. It does not diagnose, treat,
prescribe or monitor anyone. Calculators do the arithmetic entered into them and
nothing else; vial strength and diluent volume must be confirmed on the user's own
label. Serum-level curves are modelled estimates from published half-lives, not
measurements. It is for adults; the app requires an 18-or-older attestation.
Always consult a qualified healthcare provider before starting, changing, or
stopping any medical protocol.
